name: IVIS Restaurant Menu Manager
author: IVIS MEDIA Berlin

sections.description:
IVIS Restaurant Menu Manager is a comprehensive solution for restaurants, cafes, and food businesses to create and manage beautiful, professional menus on WordPress. Built with modern best practices, accessibility, and multilingual support in mind.

Key Features

  • Drag-and-Drop Menu Builder – Easily organize your menu with an intuitive interface
  • Multiple Menus – Create separate menus for lunch, dinner, drinks, etc.
  • Multilingual Ready – Built-in multilingual support plus WPML compatibility
  • Categories & Subcategories – Hierarchical organization with filtering
  • Allergen Management – Track and display allergens with automatic numbering
  • Price Variants – Support for sizes, portions, and price adjustments
  • Bulk Tools – Import and export menus and items via CSV or JSON
  • AJAX Search – Fast, powerful search across menu items
  • Schema.org – SEO-friendly structured data for better search visibility
  • Responsive Design – Mobile-first, works perfectly on all devices
  • Accessibility – Keyboard controls, dialog focus management and screen reader labels
  • Gutenberg Blocks – Native WordPress block editor support

Multilingual Support

  • Built-in integrated multilingual system (no plugins needed!)
  • WPML compatible for enterprise sites
  • Fully internationalised, ready for community translations on translate.wordpress.org
  • Translate menus, items, categories, and allergens
  • Auto-detects WordPress language settings

Display Options

  • Responsive list layout
  • Category filters
  • Allergen and additive legends
  • Search functionality
  • Custom styling options
  • Theme integration

Developer Friendly

  • Clean, well-documented code
  • Extensive hooks and filters
  • Template override system
  • REST API endpoints
  • Follows WordPress coding standards

Languages

The plugin is fully internationalised. Translations are delivered through
translate.wordpress.org, where any locale can be contributed.

  • English (en_US) – Default
  • German (de_DE)

Additional Information

Support

For support, documentation, and feature requests, please visit the plugin support forum.

Privacy

This plugin does not send your site data to external servers for analytics or marketing. Menu content is stored in your WordPress database like posts and pages. If you remove the plugin, your menus and settings are kept by default. To have everything removed on uninstall, enable “Delete all data when uninstalling” under Restaurant Menus → Settings → Management first.

Backups and updates

The complete JSON export contains plugin-owned menus, dishes, categories, additives, allergens, stored settings and integrated translations. It includes image references, not the image files. Back up the database and uploads directory separately, especially when using WPML or another external translation plugin.

JSON import is additive: existing menus and dishes are retained and new copies are created. Matching terms are reused; conflicting terms receive a separate imported copy. Plugin settings are replaced only if you select the settings checkbox. Images are matched by file path and SHA-256 digest; missing image files are reported and never mapped solely by a cross-site numeric ID. Restore the media library separately before importing on another site. Older complete JSON backups remain supported.

Updating, deactivating or uninstalling this plugin does not delete its data. Uninstalling removes it only if you enable “Delete all data when uninstalling” beforehand. Legacy shortcode aliases and template override paths remain supported.

Credits

Developed by IVIS MEDIA Berlin
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/ivis-restaurant-menu-manager, or install through the WordPress plugins screen
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress
  3. Go to Restaurant Menus → Settings to configure options
  4. Create your first menu at Restaurant Menus → Add New
sections.faq:
How do I display a menu on my site?

Use the shortcode [armm_menu id="123"] (replace 123 with your menu ID) or use the “Restaurant Menu” Gutenberg block in the block editor.

Can I have menus in multiple languages?

Yes! The plugin includes built-in multilingual support. You can also use WPML for more advanced translation workflows.

How do I manage allergens?

Go to Restaurant Menus → Allergens to add allergens. Each allergen gets an automatic alphabetical label (A, B, C, etc.).

Is the plugin accessible?

The category dialog and image lightbox support keyboard controls, Escape, focus management and screen reader labels. Accessibility also depends on the theme, colors and your content; no WCAG compliance certification is claimed.

Can I customize the design?

Yes! You can use custom CSS, choose between theme or plugin styles, and override templates by copying them to your theme folder.

Does it work with page builders?

Yes! Use the shortcode in any page builder that supports WordPress shortcodes.

Can I disable standalone menu URLs?

Yes. Under Restaurant Menus → Settings → General, turn off Public Menu Pages. Standalone menu URLs and the menu archive then return a 404, and menus are excluded from WordPress search and the core sitemap. Embedded shortcodes and blocks, editing and saved contents keep working. This setting is enabled by default to preserve existing links. Enable it again to restore the same URLs; no manual permalink flush is needed. Individual dish and taxonomy pages are unaffected.

Can I import/export menu items?

Yes! Use Restaurant Menus → Settings → Import/Export to import/export menu items via CSV.

Does the plugin include a shopping cart or checkout?

No. This version focuses on menu display, search, filters, and structured data. Ecommerce cart and checkout are not included.
sections.changelog:
1.0.12

  • Compatibility: tested with WordPress 7.2.
  • New: on WordPress 7.2 the admin menu uses a new SVG outline icon that matches the new admin icon set. Older WordPress versions keep the Dashicon.
  • Tweak: the Restaurant Menu block uses the same icon in the inserter and placeholder.
  • Tweak: block settings use the current control sizes, which removes deprecation notices in the browser console.

1.0.11

  • Fix: on multisite, activating the plugin on a single site no longer migrates data or roles on other sites of the network. Network activation sets up every site; single-site activation only touches the site it runs on.

1.0.10

  • Code quality: the plugin’s PHP constants now use the plugin prefix (ADVANCED_RESTAURANT_MENU_MANAGER_*) instead of the short ARMM_ prefix. No data or behaviour changes.

1.0.9

  • Security hardening: menu item variants, item translations and the Menu Builder structure now validate every submitted value as a scalar before unslashing and sanitizing it. The Menu Builder JSON is size- and depth-limited and rejected when malformed.

1.0.8

  • Rename: the plugin is now “IVIS Restaurant Menu Manager” with the slug and text domain ivis-restaurant-menu-manager. Post types, taxonomies, option names, capabilities, roles, block names and shortcodes are unchanged, so menus, menu items, categories, additives, allergens and settings carry over untouched.
  • Fix: the two blocks referenced a stylesheet handle that was never registered, so their “style” entry had no effect. The frontend stylesheet was still loaded by the plugin itself, so no styling was lost.
  • Data safety: deleting the plugin no longer removes your content unless you explicitly tick “Delete all data when uninstalling” on the settings screen. Previously removal was the default.
  • All admin JavaScript is enqueued through wp_enqueue_script() instead of being printed as inline script blocks on the settings screen and in the pricing, variants, translation, additive and allergen meta boxes.
  • The additive and allergen meta boxes no longer hide each other’s panels when you switch tabs.
  • Translations are no longer bundled: WordPress serves them from translate.wordpress.org, so load_plugin_textdomain() was removed.
  • The public read-only REST routes validate and sanitise their id parameters, and document why they are intentionally unauthenticated.
  • The PHP and WordPress requirement notices are shown only to users who can act on them.

1.0.6

  • New: optional public menu pages and archive, enabled by default for existing links. Disabling leaves embedded menus and contents intact and automatically refreshes URL rules; the setting is included in backups.
  • Data safety: migration waits for other plugins to register their types, avoids generic price-based ownership, keeps IDs and metadata, and journals legacy slug changes. Ambiguous legacy rows are preserved for review.
  • WPML: migration supports tables with different collations and does not mark failed migrations complete.
  • Security: custom public endpoints, shortcodes and schema exclude nonpublic and password-protected content. Authorized previews remain supported.
  • Schema: embedded menus, visible items, translations, duplicate dishes, per-menu titles, variant prices and zero price overrides reflect the rendered menu.
  • Backups: complete stored settings, term translations and descriptions, category images, privacy and media identities. Restore creates new posts and preserves existing terms and display orders; unresolved references are reported.
  • Accessibility: keyboard-accessible image buttons and modal dialogs with focus containment, Escape and focus restoration. Multiple menus have independent controls and search requests.
  • Compatibility: explicit CSV escape parameters for PHP 8.4; updated documentation, full GPL license text and actual directory screenshots.

1.0.5

  • Fix: dragging a category into a menu failed for users with the Restaurant Menu Admin role. The handler checked a core capability that the role no longer carries since 1.0.4.
  • Fix: rows added to the Menu Builder by drag and drop were always shown in English, while rows already stored in the menu were translated.
  • Fix: a stray closing div was emitted in the menu template when the search field, the category filters and the language switcher were all disabled.
  • Fix: the price hints in the Menu Builder showed a hard-coded euro sign instead of the configured currency symbol and position.
  • Fix: the AJAX search endpoint returned a PHP error instead of a clean response when the query parameter arrived as an array.
  • Fix: menu item search returned nothing at all. The taxonomy-aware part of the search was spliced into WordPress’ own search SQL on the assumption that it ended with a closing parenthesis. It does not — it ends with “) ” and, for logged-out visitors, a further password clause — so the splice left the statement with one parenthesis too many and every search failed in the database. The clause is now built in full rather than patched.
  • Fix: searching inside a menu returned items belonging to other menus. The menu_id parameter was accepted by both the AJAX and the REST search endpoint and then ignored, and the search field never sent it. Search from a menu is now limited to that menu; the standalone search shortcode still searches everything.
  • Fix: the search filter stayed attached to any query that ran while a menu search was in progress, so an unrelated query started from a hook could come back with the taxonomy join grafted on.
  • Change: the REST search endpoint now lets WordPress build its query instead of assembling one by hand. Excerpts are searched alongside titles and descriptions, and a query of several words matches items that contain all of them rather than only that exact phrase.
  • Fix: menu structures saved by older versions no longer raise PHP notices when an element is missing its type.
  • Fix: the REST suggestions endpoint no longer breaks when the category taxonomy query fails.
  • Security: the language cookie is now set with HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax, and with Secure on HTTPS.
  • Security: menu item titles are escaped before being inserted into the Menu Builder markup.
  • Security: every post and term meta key the plugin owns is now registered with an explicit sanitize and authorisation callback, so values are cleaned on all write paths including WP-CLI and third-party code.
  • Performance: the block editor no longer runs a menu query on every front-end, REST and admin-ajax request.
  • i18n: the translation template covered 86 of 489 strings and has been regenerated. German is complete again, including the context-based strings for post type and taxonomy labels, which never loaded before.
  • i18n: added the JSON translation files that the block editor needs.
  • WPML: prices and the menu structure are no longer offered for translation, and term meta plus the legal text are now declared.
  • Build: fixed the Composer autoload entry that silently terminated PHPCS, restored the WordPress coding standard checks, and made the PHPUnit suite actually execute its tests.

1.0.4

  • Security: the Restaurant Menu Admin role now uses its own armm_* capabilities. Previous versions granted site-wide post capabilities, letting the role create, edit, publish and delete regular posts and manage core categories via REST and admin-ajax.
  • Fix: additives and allergens are no longer cleared on Quick Edit, Bulk Edit, REST or WP-CLI updates. Earlier versions could silently lose legally required allergen data on any programmatic save — please verify your menu items after updating.
  • Fix: schema.org output no longer declares dishes as GlutenFreeDiet based on their allergens; the mapping was inverted. Allergens are now appended to the description as “Contains: …”.
  • Fix: CSV import no longer aborts with a fatal error on empty files, blank lines, or rows whose column count differs from the header. Malformed rows are reported instead of silently dropping the import.
  • Security: CSV exports neutralise leading =, +, -, @, tab and carriage return so spreadsheet formulas cannot be injected into an exported menu.
  • Security: category background colours are validated as hex values; previously stored non-hex values are discarded on the next save.
  • Security: JSON-LD output is escaped with JSON_HEX_TAG / JSON_HEX_AMP so item titles cannot break out of the script element.
  • Fix: the update migration no longer claims posts and taxonomies of other plugins that use generic slugs such as “menu” or “menu_item”. Object caches are invalidated after migration.
  • New: menus, menu items and their taxonomy archives have real permalinks, with single-menu.php, single-menu-item.php, archive-menu.php and taxonomy-menu.php templates you can override from your theme.
  • New: the Restaurant Menu and Restaurant Menu Search blocks now appear in the block inserter with a menu picker and live preview.
  • New: prefixed shortcodes [armm_menu], [armm_menu_search] and [armm_menu_categories]. The unprefixed legacy shortcodes keep working.
  • Performance: menu rendering no longer runs one term query per item and category. A 200-item menu drops from thousands of queries to a handful.
  • Fix: the bundled German translation is now actually loaded.
  • Fix: prices use the configured currency symbol and separators instead of a hard-coded euro sign, both in PHP and JavaScript.
  • Fix: allergen labels continue past 26 entries (AA, AB, …) instead of emitting [, \ and ].
  • Hardening: rate limiting on the public search endpoints, capability and nonce checks on taxonomy meta fields, multisite-aware uninstall, and a safer bulk assign.

1.0.3

  • Complete the rename: main plugin file is now advanced-restaurant-menu-manager.php
  • Improved AJAX search behavior and result rendering
  • Hardened input sanitization and output escaping across admin and frontend
  • Menu builder refinements (collapsible sidebar categories, live drop indicators)

1.0.2

  • Rename plugin directory and identifiers to advanced-restaurant-menu-manager
  • Automatic migration for options, post types, taxonomies, and roles
  • Legacy shortcodes, blocks, and AJAX actions remain supported

1.0.1

  • Prefix custom post types and taxonomies for WordPress.org compliance
  • Automatic migration preserves existing menu data on update
  • Align plugin header PHP requirement with readme (8.0)

1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • Drag-and-drop menu builder
  • Multiple menu support
  • Multilingual (integrated + WPML)
  • Category and allergen management
  • AJAX search
  • Add menu everywhere with a shortcode
  • REST API
  • Complete English & German translation
  • Keyboard navigation and screen reader labels
  • Schema.org structured data
  • Import/Export via CSV & JSON
  • Custom user role management

upgrade_notice.1.0.6: Back up your database and uploads, then update in place. Do not uninstall first. Existing content and IDs are retained; 1.0.5 needs no schema migration. Ambiguous older records are preserved for review.
